findings.summary: A tagged union whose arm field has no representation no longer degrades to its common-field struct: the discriminated mapper signals the failure and the union has no representation, so the refusal lands at the unrepresented field instead of at a literal spelling it; a compiler test pins the true site.

The absent-member rule of the nullable-union branch also recognizes an intersection the checker distributed null or undefined into (`S & undefined`), which is what narrowing `S | null` past a null check produces; the recognizer's `{} | undefined` arm never fired and is gone, and `object` counts as a non-null constraint.
The intersection arm's condition and comment are minimal: one remaining constituent maps under the substitution.

Two registry helpers, `absentValue` and `presentValue`, own the nullable spelling (an empty optional or the null reference of a shared object) at the conditional record, the guarded-and-null sink arm, the hit record and the optional element result, which each spelled it inline.

The lone-member shortcut of the nullable-union branch stays for the record-source registration it performs, and its comment says so instead of claiming to protect a binding the intersection arm now maps.

For an array whose element type admits null, a reference-struct element's own presence answers `saves[i] === null` alone (the accessor yields the null reference out of range as well), one check instead of two; arrays of non-null elements keep the index check and their generated code, so six demos that had moved are byte-identical again; truthiness defaults to that presence instead of comparing generated strings.

The fixture keeps the shapes that pin the change (a generic plan through a reference-backed intent, a generic pick, a null element passed, compared and tested directly) and drops the tag field, the redundant guard chain and the untouched flag.
The lone-member shortcut could collapse into `fromTsType(getNonNullableType(type))` now that the intersection arm maps NonNullable<T>.
findings.blockedBy: The shortcut registers the lone member as its own record source, which the general path does not, and the swap needs a corpus-wide neutrality proof.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md (the classification consolidation entry: one owner for the nullable-union member rule)

findings.summary: A value-typed parameter narrowed past null inside an object literal still refuses "Conditional record property must have one non-optional native data type", because the shorthand keeps the parameter's nullable representation.
findings.blockedBy: Narrowing the shorthand needs the flow type under the call's substitution: the checker's `(S & undefined) | (S & {})` admits undefined until S is bound.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md (Functions limits: a value-typed parameter narrowed past null keeps its nullable representation inside an object literal)

findings.summary: The Map iterator's `next().value` keeps the index-only presence for a reference-struct value, the pattern the element read left behind.
findings.blockedBy: The map value type's nullability is not recoverable at that site (the registry collapses an optional reference struct to the struct) and no scene iterates a map of nullable references.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md (Map/Set limits: an iterator value of a nullable reference type reads as present)
